subject: Data residency & export Qs — access/audit log retention buckets
messages:
From: Alice Martin <alice.martin@finvero.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:14:00Z
Subject: Questions on access/audit log exports and residency

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. A couple of follow-ups from our InfoSec & compliance team about audit/access logs:

1) Retention: What are the default retention windows for access logs vs audit logs in the hosted product? Are there fixed tiers or can we request custom retention for an enterprise contract?
2) Residency: If we require EU-only storage, will exported logs reflect EU residency? Is there any cross-region replication of audit/access logs we should be aware of?
3) Export formats and delivery: Which export formats do you support (syslog, JSON, CSV)? Can exports be delivered to our SFTP/GCS/Azure storage?
4) Deletion & GDPR: If a user deletion request hits our app, and their identifiers appear in audit/log exports taken earlier, what controls do we provide to purge those exported artifacts?

We're trying to map this into our SOC scope and would appreciate a short written summary and a sample export so our auditors can validate the schema.

Best,
Alice Martin
Lead, Security Assurance
Finvero

[Note: copying audit-team@finvero.com for records]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Martin <alice.martin@finvero.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on access/audit log exports and residency

Hi Alice — great questions. Short answers first, followed by a few implementation notes and attachments.

- Retention (defaults & flexibility):
  * Access logs (authentication, session events): default 90 days for Hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can configure to 30 days–7 years via contract and config.
  * Audit logs (admin actions, policy changes, config changes): default 365 days for Hosted; Dedicated/Private configurable 1–7 years.
  * We can include custom retention tiers in enterprise SOWs; retention enforcement is automatic on the system side for hosted tenants.

- Residency & replication:
  * For EU-only customers, we store and process logs in our EU region by default (no cross-region replication for primary data).
  * Short-lived operational replicas (for failover) do not contain long-term audit archives; we can provide a design review for highly restricted residency needs.

- Export formats & delivery:
  * Supported formats: JSON (structured events), CSV (flat exports), and RFC5424-compatible syslog streams.
  * Delivery: SFTP (encrypted), S3/GCS/Azure blob via customer buckets or our dedicated transfer endpoints, and streamed syslog to an on-prem collector.
  * Exports may be requested ad-hoc (time-range) or scheduled (daily/weekly/monthly).

- Deletion & exported artifacts:
  * Deletion requests (e.g., GDPR erasure) affect Redwood-hosted copies according to retention policy.
  * Exports delivered to customer-controlled storage are considered external systems; Redwood cannot automatically remove copies you download.
  * To mitigate this, we offer: (a) pseudonymized exports (PII hashed) as a default option, (b) short-lived delivery windows (files retained on our transfer endpoint for X days), and (c) contractual obligations to purge server-side transfer copies on request.

I've attached a short export spec and a sample syslog extract to help your auditors (see attachments).

Attachments: redwood-audit-export-spec.pdf (summary, fields + examples)
             finvero-sample-syslog-export.csv (sample rows)

If it helps, we can schedule a 30‑minute run-through with our privacy engineer to show a live export and the pseudonymization controls.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — that's helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our auditors:

1) Pseudonymization: Does the hashing use a customer-specific salt or a Redwood-wide salt? Our auditors prefer a customer salt to avoid re-identification across customers.
2) Time-range exports: Can you confirm minimum/maximum time-range for ad-hoc exports (e.g., 1 hour to full lifetime)?
3) Retention proof: For compliance we'd like a statement about how retention enforcement is logged so we can demonstrate that records older than the retention window are not queryable. Do you provide an audit of deletion jobs?

Also — can you drop the sample CSV into the Drive folder you mentioned earlier so our team can run their parsing scripts?

Best,
Alice

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

On Tue, Aug 24, 2026 at 09:22 AM Alice Martin <alice.martin@finvero.com> wrote:
> 1) Pseudonymization: Does the hashing use a customer-specific salt or a Redwood-wide salt?
> 2) Time-range exports: Can you confirm minimum/maximum time-range for ad-hoc exports (e.g., 1 hour to full lifetime)?
> 3) Retention proof: For compliance we'd like a statement about how retention enforcement is logged so we can demonstrate that records older than the retention window are not queryable.

Hi Alice — quick clarifications:

1) Pseudonymization: We support customer-scoped salts. For enterprise accounts we generate and store a customer KMS-wrapped salt per tenant; hashes produced for exports use that salt so re-identification across tenants is not possible. This option is enabled by request and noted in the export manifest.

2) Time-range exports: Ad-hoc exports support any contiguous time-range bounded by the retention window (e.g., if your access logs retention is 90 days, you can export any slice within those 90 days). Minimum slice is 1 minute; maximum is the full retained window. For longer historical exports beyond the default retention we can provide archive pulls under an SOW.

3) Retention enforcement & proof:
  * Deletion jobs are orchestrated and recorded. We record a DeletionJob audit event (job id, scope, start/end times, affected shards) and retain that event in the audit log for contractual durations.
  * We can provide redacted deletion-job manifests and a verification snapshot (hash) to confirm deletion completion for compliance audits.

Operational notes:
- Export retention on transfer endpoints: files uploaded to our SFTP staging area are retained for 7 days by default; we can shorten or lengthen this retention in contract.
- Export copies you place in your buckets are under your control — recommend lifecycle rules to enforce purge.
- We will drop the sample CSV into the Drive folder (see link in the thread).

Next steps: would you like the privacy engineer to join a 30‑minute session next week? If yes, propose two slots and we'll lock one.

Thanks,
Jonas
